analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 533-1020). The only changed range (base 11-13, head 11-100) lies outside the supplied lines, so the units are historical changelog text with no executable code. I examined them against the threat model and found nothing to cite as a regression.

Security-relevant documentation seen in the historical text: staging and dev environment identities, an installer signature relaxation for -dev./-staging. versions, and release workflow notes; encrypted SSD cache write budgets and external-volume validation (T-041); App Attest and endpoint resumption (TB-011, T-053); logout and revocation behavior (A-008); and the fan helper (TB-010).

The patch excerpt is truncated and shows the head side adding a v0.10.1 candidate section. That section includes the claim that page-cache accounting counts more memory as available for load admission and KV budgets on every model, which may affect memory-pressure and availability assumptions. The excerpt also mentions an SDK bump, libs/mlx-swift-lm 7bed8216 to 6148b6da, and GLM logprob refusals. I cannot verify any of these from the supplied lines. A later pass should review the actual source changes behind the head-side changelog text, in particular page-cache accounting, the dependency pin and request-refusal logic (T-010, T-029, T-041).

The patch only edits documentation, so no control is shown as weakened. The dependency on a coordinator change (darkbloom-platform#411) is an external contract that I did not verify. No finding is raised.
